ryan.body_md:
# Ryan Perry

**Ryan Perry** is a software engineer and founder. He co-founded Pyroscope, an open-source continuous profiling project that Grafana Labs acquired in March 2023 [1][5][7]. He is a Senior Field Engineer at SpaceXAI and has written about running his mobile game Rank'em with a team of Grok Bot agents [1][2][3].

## Career

Perry's site lists 2014 as the year of his first tech job [1]. He writes that his first software engineering job was at Sensor Tower, a mobile app analytics company, and that he later worked at Lion Studios, part of AppLovin [2]. His writing index includes a 2019 post about a coding bootcamp he attended [1]. Y Combinator's profile says he worked at Sensor Tower and Lion Studios in software engineering, product and data engineering roles [6].

### Pyroscope and Grafana Labs

Perry and Dmitry Filimonov founded Pyroscope in 2021 [5]. It went through Y Combinator's Winter 2021 batch [6]. Grafana Labs announced the acquisition on March 15, 2023, and merged it with Grafana Phlare under the name Grafana Pyroscope [5][7]. TechCrunch quoted Perry as co-founder and CEO of Pyroscope [7]. Perry's site lists his roles as Pyroscope CEO and co-founder, then Principal Emerging Products Manager at Grafana Labs [1].

### SpaceXAI and Rank'em

Perry is a Senior Field Engineer at SpaceXAI (Luma lists the company as SpaceXSI) and has presented Grok Bot workshops, including one on pairing Grok Bot with Cursor cloud agents [1][8]. His site lists two live games: Rank'em, a party game where players rank a topic, and Clue Rush, a trivia game [1].

In an August 25, 2026, post, Perry described six bots that run Rank'em: an orchestrator that owns the App Store and Google Play listings, plus analytics, ad creative, app engineering, infrastructure and bug-fix bots [2][3]. Each has its own cloud computer, routines and connected accounts, and they hand work to each other [3]. He wrote that the game had just passed 1,000 downloads across iOS and Android over the previous week [3]. He credited the bots with cutting cost per install from $15 to about $1 after switching to an ad aimed at couples, and with about a 4x improvement in day-7 retention after a hint feature shipped [3]. His own blog version calls the retention gain "projected" and the cost-per-install gain "measured" [2].

An October 2026 post on X by @diamai_, summarizing a talk Perry gave on the official Grok channel, quoted him saying a team of bots had run the app "totally autonomously for the past, I think probably like 2 months," and said the app was at about 10,000 downloads [4]. The 10,000 figure comes from that post and was not found in Perry's own writing.
